newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share market ends flat, some upside seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share market ends flat, some upside seen.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended flat in lacklustre trade amid scattered activity in second-liner or small capitalisation stocks, dealers said on Friday.
"Most of the heavy volume is generated by second-liners and small cap stocks of less than S$1," a dealer with a European bank said.

He said sentiment for shares like Nippecraft Ltd, Fu Yu and Lindeteves-Jacoberg was firm as retail investors were hoping for a shift in interest to small capitalisation stocks in Singapore from Malaysia. Another dealer said volumes of these stocks were ramped up by syndicates and were unlikely to be sustainable.
Nippecraft topped the actives with 12.4 million shares. Fu Yu was also actively traded due to renewed interest in electronic counters, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index closed 1.90 points down at 2,148.86. Total volume was 117.6 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 174 to 149.
Continued interest was evident in Malaysian counters, with UMW Holdings among gainers, rising Singapore $0.20 to S$5.70 (US$4.04).
OUT Foreign led the losers, shedding S$1.70 to S$2.20 on 1,000 shares traded. The STII was expected to see an upside of four to six percent next week.
